key_insight: UniMedSeg unifies multiple medical image segmentation paradigms—such as visual in-context, interactive, and language-guided segmentation—into one model. It also bridges 2D and 3D segmentation, aiming to learn from heterogeneous annotations with a single scalable framework.
problem_solved: Existing medical segmentation foundation models are fragmented: different prompt types and spatial dimensions are usually handled by separate specialized systems. This limits scalability and prevents joint learning from diverse 2D/3D data and annotation formats.
method: Builds a unified in-context learning framework that can accept different prompt paradigms for segmentation.
Designs the model to handle both 2D and 3D medical images within a shared representation space.
Targets multi-paradigm training so heterogeneous labels and prompts can contribute to one general-purpose segmentation model.
impact: This could simplify deployment in clinical AI by reducing the need for separate models for each segmentation task or input style. For practitioners, it offers a more flexible path toward foundation models that generalize across datasets, organs, modalities, and annotation types.

paper_title: UniMedSeg: Unified In-Context Learning for Multi-Paradigm 2D/3D Medical Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Yunzhou Li, Jiesi Hu, Yanwu Yang, Hanyang Peng, Chenfei Ye
